<div class="hero">
  <p class="eyebrow">Applied Development Economics Research Dashboard</p>
  <h1>Structural Vulnerability in Latin America and the Caribbean</h1>
  <h2>An OECD-style research dashboard for applied development economics</h2>
  <p class="abstract">This dashboard summarizes descriptive and econometric evidence from a harmonized country-year panel covering poverty, labor informality, social protection, macroeconomic conditions, and structural vulnerability in Latin America and the Caribbean.</p>
</div>

## Key Indicators

<div class="kpi-grid">
  <div class="kpi-card"><span class="kpi-value">27</span><span class="kpi-label">Countries</span></div>
  <div class="kpi-card"><span class="kpi-value">2000-2023</span><span class="kpi-label">Years</span></div>
  <div class="kpi-card"><span class="kpi-value">648</span><span class="kpi-label">Country-year observations</span></div>
  <div class="kpi-card"><span class="kpi-value">178</span><span class="kpi-label">Analytical sample</span></div>
  <div class="kpi-card"><span class="kpi-value">17</span><span class="kpi-label">Countries in econometric sample</span></div>
  <div class="kpi-card"><span class="kpi-value">SVI</span><span class="kpi-label">Main outcome</span></div>
</div>

## Research Question

<div class="callout-box">
How do poverty, labor informality, and social protection jointly shape structural vulnerability across Latin America and the Caribbean?
</div>

## Main Findings

<div class="finding-grid">
  <div class="finding-card">Labor informality is positively associated with structural vulnerability in the TWFE specification.</div>
  <div class="finding-card">Social protection coverage is negatively associated with structural vulnerability.</div>
  <div class="finding-card">GDP per capita is negatively associated with vulnerability, while unemployment and inequality are positively associated with vulnerability.</div>
  <div class="finding-card">Results should be interpreted as associational, not causal, because the index and regressors are conceptually related and endogeneity remains possible.</div>
</div>

## Econometric Evidence

![Two-Way Fixed Effects Estimates](../outputs/figures/oecd_style/figure_07_model_coefficients.svg){.dashboard-figure}

![Observed and Predicted Structural Vulnerability](../outputs/figures/oecd_style/figure_08_predicted_vs_observed.svg){.dashboard-figure}

| Variable | TWFE coefficient | p-value |
|---|---:|---:|
| labor_informality | 0.0103 | <0.001 |
| social_protection_coverage | -0.0102 | <0.001 |
| gdp_per_capita_1000 | -0.0219 | 0.0388 |
| unemployment | 0.0537 | <0.001 |
| gini | 0.0359 | <0.001 |
| R-squared | 0.9977 |  |

<p class="note-box">These estimates are associational and should not be interpreted as causal effects.</p>

## Data Quality

![Indicator Coverage and Missingness](../outputs/figures/oecd_style/figure_09_missingness_map.svg){.dashboard-figure}

<p class="interpretation">Missingness varies by indicator and year. The analytical sample is narrower than the full panel because econometric specifications require jointly observed values.</p>

## Research Pipeline

![Research Pipeline](../outputs/figures/oecd_style/figure_10_research_pipeline.svg){.dashboard-figure}

## Policy Interpretation

<div class="callout-box">
Policy strategies should address overlapping vulnerabilities rather than poverty alone. The descriptive and econometric evidence points to the importance of formal employment, social protection coverage, macroeconomic capacity, and inequality reduction.
</div>

## Footer

<div class="footer-note">
Data sources: harmonized country-year panel based on SEDLAC, WDI, ILOSTAT, ASPIRE, and CEPALSTAT source families.<br>
Repository: structural-vulnerability-lac-research.<br>
Interpretation: descriptive and associational evidence only.
</div>
